sources.entry: blocky - Fast and lightweight DNS proxy as ad-blocker for local network with many features (alternative to Pi-hole). (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Blocky is a DNS proxy and ad-blocker for the local network, written in Go, that filters queries with external blocklists and can serve as an alternative to Pi-hole.
summary.what_it_does: Blocky blocks DNS queries using external allow/denylists, configurable per client group, with periodic reload and regex support. It can also block based on the request domain, response CNAME (deep CNAME inspection), and response IP addresses. Beyond blocking, it offers custom DNS resolution for specific domains, conditional forwarding to external DNS servers, and per-group upstream resolvers. It caches answers and prefetches frequently used queries, and can query multiple upstream resolvers at once. It serves DNS over UDP/TCP, DoH, DoT, DoQ, and DoH3, and provides a DoH endpoint, along with Prometheus metrics, query logging (CSV or MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL/Timescale), REST API endpoints, and a CLI tool.
use_cases: block ads and malware across the home network
per-device or per-group filtering for kids or smart home devices
custom DNS entries and conditional forwarding for a homelab
encrypted DNS server with DoH, DoT, or DoQ
replace Pi-hole on a Raspberry Pi or OpenWrt router
monitor DNS query metrics with Prometheus and Grafana
run DNS filtering in Kubernetes via community Helm chart
how_to_run: Follow the Installation chapter in the full documentation (link not included in the README text)
Docker image with multi-arch support is available
notable: Stateless design: no database or temporary files required
Supports DoH, DoT, DoQ, and DoH3 in addition to plain DNS
Deep CNAME inspection and IP-list blocking of responses
Runs on x86-64, ARM, and MIPS including Raspberry Pi and OpenWrt
Claims no telemetry or user data collection
caveats: Full installation and configuration details are only in the external documentation, not the README
Kubernetes deployment relies on a community-supported Helm chart
The README asks for financial support from users to fund development
